Under [r-task-phase-needs-wave], a task in a phase inherits that phase’s needs, so this is wrong whenever the found item’s phase has prerequisites. chunk_findings.detail: The fix task is still created with `needs=[]`, even when it inherits prerequisites from its phase. The new `no_deps` boolean only suppresses the `no-deps` tag when `inherited_deps(st, st.items[parent], cfg)` is nonempty; it never writes those inherited dependencies into the task’s `needs`. Example: phase `P1` has `needs=["P0"]`, and `bug_found(..., item="T1")` is called for `T1` under `P1`. `parent` is `P1`, `no_deps` is `False`, so the task is filed under `P1` with `needs=[]` and no `no-deps` tag. Under [r-task-phase-needs-wave], every task must state its dependencies in `needs`; a task in a phase with prerequisites is not accurately described by an empty `needs` list, and any consumer reading `.needs` for claimability or wave stamping can still treat it as prerequisite-free. The change answers the old `no-deps`-tag half but not the empty-`needs` half of the previous finding.

data.probe: needs=[] is CORRECT, not an omission: the fix task declares no DIRECT prerequisite of its own; its phase's needs are INHERITED by inherited_deps (core/schedule/_readiness.py: 'A phase is never claimed; only its tasks are... a readiness rule reading it.needs and stopping there makes every phase-level dependency decorative'), never copied into the task's own needs. Readiness and wave stamping read inherited_deps (which already adds every ancestor phase's needs), so a claim reads P0 as a prerequisite regardless of the task's empty needs. Writing P0 into the task's needs would double-count it (it is the phase's dependency, not the task's)
